neighbours.label: The reassurance or acceptance formula: 'no problem', 'that's fine', 'very well', 'no worries', 'kein Problem', at the word that completes it; quiet on the same words used literally.
fire: The bus is full? No problem, we can walk to the station from here.
"Sorry, I'll be ten minutes late," he texted. "That's fine, take your time," she replied.
The captain heard the sailor's plea and said, "Very well, you may go ashore."
You lost the receipt, but no worries, we can look it up in the system.
Keine Zeit am Montag? Kein Problem, wir verschieben den Termin.
If you want to bring a friend along, that's fine with us.
"Can you cover my shift?" "Sure, no problem."
She asked to leave early, and the manager nodded: "Very well."
quiet: The bus is full because a problem with the trains closed the line.
"Sorry, I'll be ten minutes late," he texted, and she wrote back that the sand was fine and soft.
The captain heard the sailor sing very well during the long night watch.
You lost the receipt, and your worries about the refund were justified.
Keine Zeit am Montag, weil das Problem mit dem Auto noch besteht.
If you want to bring a friend along, the fine print says guests pay extra.
"Can you cover my shift?" "The problem is that I work that day too."
She asked to leave early because the well in the village had run dry.

predictions: median fire ~0.7 (probes: No problem 0.96, Kein Problem 1.17, Very well 0.69, no worries 0.68, That's fine 0.63); near misses < 0.05 (literal problem 0.007-0.01, 'did well... felt fine' 0.02).
notes: Card top: Kein Problem, No problem, Very well, That's fine, no worries, 当然沒問題. The distinction is speech-act (granting/reassuring) vs literal use of the same words.
